specAnchors.text: understand the effects on crop yield of increased carbon dioxide and increased temperature in glasshouses

primer.text: Three dials govern how fast a crop photosynthesises: temperature, light intensity and carbon dioxide concentration. This note explains what happens when each dial is turned up, why every dial eventually hits a ceiling, and how glasshouse growers exploit that knowledge to lift crop yields.

modules.title: Three Dials That Decide the Harvest
sourceHeadings: Crop Plants: Increasing Carbon Dioxide & Temperature
modules.opening: A plant with unlimited light, carbon dioxide and warmth would photosynthesise as fast as its chemistry allows, but real crops always run short of one input. Whatever is scarcest caps the rate, so raising temperature, light intensity or carbon dioxide concentration lifts photosynthesis — until another factor becomes the bottleneck.
keyPoints: Temperature, light intensity and carbon dioxide concentration are the three main limiting factors for photosynthesis.
Warming raises the rate because enzymes drive the reaction, but beyond a ceiling the enzymes denature and the rate collapses.
Brighter light speeds photosynthesis until some other input runs short.
Extra carbon dioxide accelerates the reaction because it is a raw material, again until another factor limits.

low.restatement: More warmth, more light, more carbon dioxide — each speeds the plant up until something else runs out.
low.analogy: Three taps feeding one bucket: the slowest tap decides the flow, and opening one tap only helps while it stays the slowest.
low.examPointer: Say what happens past the temperature ceiling — enzymes denature — because that turn of the curve earns the second mark.

medium.restatement: Photosynthesis is capped by whichever input is scarcest; raising temperature speeds the enzyme-driven reaction until denaturation reverses the trend, while increasing light intensity or carbon dioxide concentration raises the rate until a different factor becomes limiting in turn.
medium.analogy: A relay team whose slowest runner sets the pace; swapping in a faster runner helps only until another runner becomes the slowest.
medium.examPointer: For glasshouse questions, connect each factor to a control: heaters for temperature, lamps for light, carbon dioxide enrichment for concentration.

glossary.definition: Whatever input is scarcest, capping the rate of photosynthesis at that moment.
The permanent shape change that destroys an enzyme's working surface at high temperature.
How bright the light falling on a leaf is.
